construct: The proximal tubule metabolizes glutamine to generate ammonium and bicarbonate. During metabolic acidosis, renal ammoniagenesis and urinary ammonium excretion increase. Excretion of the generated ammonium allows the concurrently generated bicarbonate to represent net new bicarbonate returned to the systemic circulation.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Persistent metabolic acidosis stimulates proximal-tubule glutamine catabolism, increasing ammonium generation/excretion while returning newly generated bicarbonate to blood.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Increasing renal glutamine synthesis from ammonium is the strongest metabolic-direction distractor, but it consumes rather than generates the ammonium needed for enhanced acid excretion.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Only increased glutamine ammoniagenesis simultaneously explains the rise in urinary NH4+ and generation of new systemic bicarbonate.
